full_row.wylie: des na, las can gyi 'gro ba gsum gyis brlan zhing gsher ba phor pa gang la cig car du bltas pa de'i tshe, tshad mtshungs nges par dgos pa ma yin te, dgos na, phor pa gang po de'i nang du gnas kyi blos gnas shing , tha mal gyi mig shes kyis mi bzod pa'i srog chags phra mo'i mig shes kyis kyang , de'i tshad mar 'gro dgos pa dang , rgya mtsho'i nang na gnas pa'i srog chags phra mo'i mig shes kyis kyang , rgya mtsho'i tshad la tshad mar 'gro dgos pa dang , lha ma yin 'ga' zhig la, mtshon cha phor gang snang dgos pa la sogs pa'i skyon yod pa'i phyir
full_row.english: In conclusion now, let us consider again these three kinds of beings, each with their different karma, as they sit down together and look at a glass full of something wet and flowing. It's not necessarily true that they must all have valid perceptions which are identical. If they did, then the three beings looking at the glass of water would have to think of the water as a place to live, in the way that a creature living in water would. The three beings as well would have to see the water in the same way that microscopic organisms living in the water, little beings imperceptible to normal visual consciousness, see it with their own visual consciousness. Then too the visual consciousness of microscopic organisms living in the depths of the ocean would have to be a valid perception towards the entire extent of the sea. And certain kinds of near-gods too would have to see weapons as glasses of water, and on and on; the problems raised would be many.

archive_object.wylie: des na, las can gyi 'gro ba gsum gyis brlan zhing gsher ba phor pa gang la cig car du bltas pa de'i tshe, tshad mtshungs nges par dgos pa ma yin te, dgos na, phor pa gang po de'i nang du gnas kyi blos gnas shing , tha mal gyi mig shes kyis mi bzod pa'i srog chags phra mo'i mig shes kyis kyang , de'i tshad mar 'gro dgos pa dang , rgya mtsho'i nang na gnas pa'i srog chags phra mo'i mig shes kyis kyang , rgya mtsho'i tshad la tshad mar 'gro dgos pa dang , lha ma yin 'ga' zhig la, mtshon cha phor gang snang dgos pa la sogs pa'i skyon yod pa'i phyir
archive_object.english: In conclusion now, let us consider again these three kinds of beings, each with their different karma, as they sit down together and look at a glass full of something wet and flowing. It's not necessarily true that they must all have valid perceptions which are identical. If they did, then the three beings looking at the glass of water would have to think of the water as a place to live, in the way that a creature living in water would. The three beings as well would have to see the water in the same way that microscopic organisms living in the water, little beings imperceptible to normal visual consciousness, see it with their own visual consciousness. Then too the visual consciousness of microscopic organisms living in the depths of the ocean would have to be a valid perception towards the entire extent of the sea. And certain kinds of near-gods too would have to see weapons as glasses of water, and on and on; the problems raised would be many.

full_row.acip: RNAG LA SOGS PA'I DNGOS PO GSUM PO DE SPYIR GO SA 'GOG NUS KYI DNGOS PO YIN KYANG , DE LTAR BLTAS PA DE'I TSE NA GO SA 'GOG BYED KYI DNGOS PO MA YIN PA MI 'GAL TE, RI RAB GRU BZHI DANG , ZLUM PO LA SOGS PA PHAN TSUN GO SA 'GOG NUS KYI DNGOS PO YIN KYANG , RI RAB GCIG GI GO SA NA, DE GNYIS KA YOD PA SRID PA LTA BU YIN PA'I PHYIR, LCAGS GONG DMAR 'BAR BA TSA BA YIN KYANG , LCAGS SNGAGS BTAB PA'I LAG PAS REG PA'I TSE, DE'I MYONG BYAR GYUR PA'I REG BYA DE TSA BA'I REG BYA MA YIN TE, TSA BA MA YIN PA'I REG BYA YIN PA'I PHYIR,
full_row.wylie: rnag la sogs pa'i dngos po gsum po de spyir go sa 'gog nus kyi dngos po yin kyang , de ltar bltas pa de'i tshe na go sa 'gog byed kyi dngos po ma yin pa mi 'gal te, ri rab gru bzhi dang , zlum po la sogs pa phan tshun go sa 'gog nus kyi dngos po yin kyang , ri rab gcig gi go sa na, de gnyis ka yod pa srid pa lta bu yin pa'i phyir, lcags gong dmar 'bar ba tsha ba yin kyang , lcags sngags btab pa'i lag pas reg pa'i tshe, de'i myong byar gyur pa'i reg bya de tsha ba'i reg bya ma yin te, tsha ba ma yin pa'i reg bya yin pa'i phyir
full_row.english: Generally speaking, each of the three objects mentioned--the pus and the other two--are things of the type that block other objects from entering into the space which they themselves occupy. It is no contradiction though to say that, in this situation where the beings are looking this way, they are not objects such that they block other things from entering into the space they occupy. This is true for the following reason. A central mountain of the world which is square in shape, and a central mountain of the world which is round in shape, and the like, are objects such that they block other things from entering the space they occupy. Nevertheless, it is possible for both these things to occupy the space taken up by a single central mountain of the world. A red-hot ball of steel is something that's hot, but consider what happens when a person touches it after he has used the mantra of steel on his hand. The sensation that he feels is not a sensation of heat; on the contrary, it is a sensation of something not heat. 35 Three Types of Each Path of Action

full_row.acip: CHOS THAMS CAD RTOG PAS BTAGS PA'I DPE NI, THAG PA KHRA BO YUL MI GSAL BA NA GNAS PA'I TSE KHA CIG LA 'DI SBRUL LO SNYAM PA'I BLO 'BYUNG NGO , , DE'I TSE THAG PA DE'I TSOGS PA DANG CHA SHAS GANG YANG SBRUL DU MED KYANG , DE LA SBRUL LO SNYAM PA'I SBRUL NI RTOG PAS BTAGS PA TZAM DU 'CHAR RO,
full_row.wylie: chos thams cad rtog pas btags pa'i dpe ni, thag pa khra bo yul mi gsal ba na gnas pa'i tshe kha cig la 'di sbrul lo snyam pa'i blo 'byung ngo , , de'i tshe thag pa de'i tshogs pa dang cha shas gang yang sbrul du med kyang , de la sbrul lo snyam pa'i sbrul ni rtog pas btags pa tsam du 'char ro
full_row.english: There is a metaphor used to describe how all existing things are labelled with our concepts. When you put a rope with a checkered pattern on it in a dark corner, some people might get the impression that it's a snake. The truth at this point though is that nothing about the rope is a snake: neither the rope as a whole, nor the parts of the rope. Nonetheless the person thinks of the rope as a snake, and this snake is an example of something which only makes its appearance as something labelled with a concept.

full_row.acip: ,DE BZHIN DU PHUNG PO 'DI LA BRTEN NAS NGA'O SNYAM DU 'BYUNG YANG , PHUNG PO'I TSOGS PA DANG RGYUN DANG CHA SHAS GANG YANG NGA'I MTSAN GZHIR 'JOG RGYU MED CING , PHUNG PO LAS NGO BO THA DAD PA GZHAN ZHIG KYANG NGA'I MTSAN GZHIR BZUNG MED PAS, NGA DE NI PHUNG PO LA BRTEN NAS BTAGS PA TZAM YIN GYI, RANG GI NGO BO NYID KYIS GRUB PA MED DO,
full_row.wylie: de bzhin du phung po 'di la brten nas nga'o snyam du 'byung yang , phung po'i tshogs pa dang rgyun dang cha shas gang yang nga'i mtshan gzhir 'jog rgyu med cing , phung po las ngo bo tha dad pa gzhan zhig kyang nga'i mtshan gzhir bzung med pas, nga de ni phung po la brten nas btags pa tsam yin gyi, rang gi ngo bo nyid kyis grub pa med do
full_row.english: In the same way, the heaps of parts that make us up serve as a basis for us to get the impression "This is me." There is nothing at all about these heaps as a whole, nor their continuation over time, nor their separate components, that we could establish as being an actual representation of "me." At the same time though there is nothing else, nothing essentially separate from these heaps of parts to ourselves, that we could consider an actual representation of "me" either. As such, this "me" is merely something labelled upon the heaps of parts that make us up; there is nothing which exists by its own essence. ************

full_row.acip: ,RGYU MTSAN NI, 'TSANG RGYA BA'I GNAS KYI ZHING GI BKOD PA PHUN SUM TSOGS PA RNAMS NI RGYU RKYEN DU MA TSOGS NAS BYUNG BA SGYU MA LTA BU'I BKOD PA YIN GYI, DON DAM PAR BKOD PA DE DAG MED PAR DE BZHIN GSHEGS PAS GSUNGS PA'I PHYIR TE, 'ON KYANG MA BRTAG MA DPYAD PA'I BLO NGO NA YOD PAS THA SNYAD DU ZHING GI BKOD PA RNAMS ZHES BYA'O, , SANGS RGYAS KYI ZHING MA ZAD, SNOD BCUD KYI BKOD PA THAMS CAD KYANG CHA SHAS DU MA TSOGS PA LA BTAGS PA STE, KHANG PA LA SOGS PA BZHIN NO, , DE DAG THAMS CAD KYANG RIGS PAS RDUL PHRA RAB KYI BAR BSHIG NA CI YANG MA YIN PA'I BAR 'GYUR TE MTSON TZAM MO,
full_row.wylie: rgyu mtshan ni, 'tshang rgya ba'i gnas kyi zhing gi bkod pa phun sum tshogs pa rnams ni rgyu rkyen du ma tshogs nas byung ba sgyu ma lta bu'i bkod pa yin gyi, don dam par bkod pa de dag med par de bzhin gshegs pas gsungs pa'i phyir te, 'on kyang ma brtag ma dpyad pa'i blo ngo na yod pas tha snyad du zhing gi bkod pa rnams zhes bya'o, , sangs rgyas kyi zhing ma zad, snod bcud kyi bkod pa thams cad kyang cha shas du ma tshogs pa la btags pa ste, khang pa la sogs pa bzhin no, , de dag thams cad kyang rigs pas rdul phra rab kyi bar bshig na ci yang ma yin pa'i bar 'gyur te mtshon tsam mo
full_row.english: Why is this the case? The reason is that the Ones Thus Gone have stated that these perfect paradises, these places where you achieve your enlightenment, are put there like an illusion; that is, they occur because a great many causes and conditions have come together. But lands which have been put there in an ultimate sense, say the Buddhas, do not even exist. Since though they do exist to that state of mind which performs no check or analysis, we can nominally call them "paradise." This fact refers not only to the paradise of a Buddha, but also to each and every thing which has ever been put here: to both the world where beings live and the beings who live in the world. All of these are simply a label put on the collection of a number of parts: they are all the same as a house, for example. And all of these are such that, should you break them down mentally all the way to their tiniest atoms, you would reach the point where they are nothing at all. (This is the briefest sketch of the meaning for you.) ************ 17 The Emptiness of Every Object

full_row.acip: ,'O NA KHYOD RANG GI LUGS JI LTAR YIN ZHE NA PHUNG PO'I RGYUN GCIG LA NI BRTEN SU LAS BYED PA PO DANG 'BRAS BU SPYOD PA PO ZHES BYA BAR BSTAN PA STE BDAGS SO, , RGYUN ZHES PA NI CHA SHAS SU GYUR PA'I SKAD CIG SNGA PHYI BAR GSUM NYE BAR BLANG BYAR YOD PA'I CHA CAN NYE BAR LEN PA PO STE MDOR NA GANG ZAG 'DIS LAS KYANG BYAS 'BRAS BU YANG MYONG ZHES PA 'THAD KYI RGYU 'BRAS DUS GCIG PA SUS KYANG BZHAG MI NUS SO,
full_row.wylie: 'o na khyod rang gi lugs ji ltar yin zhe na phung po'i rgyun gcig la ni brten su las byed pa po dang 'bras bu spyod pa po zhes bya bar bstan pa ste bdags so, , rgyun zhes pa ni cha shas su gyur pa'i skad cig snga phyi bar gsum nye bar blang byar yod pa'i cha can nye bar len pa po ste mdor na gang zag 'dis las kyang byas 'bras bu yang myong zhes pa 'thad kyi rgyu 'bras dus gcig pa sus kyang bzhag mi nus so
full_row.english: "Well then," you may continue, "what is your own position in this regard?" We can point to someone as--that is, name someone as--"the one who performs the karma" and "the one who experiences the result" all with reference to a single continuous stream of the parts or heaps to a person. The term "continuous stream" here refers to a whole, the person to whom the various parts belong; and these parts are the moments of them that exist earlier, later, and in between, and which belong to the person. To summarize, it is entirely correct to say that any one person has both committed a karma and experienced its consequences; it's not the case though that cause and effect are then simultaneous--no one could ever show that was the case.

full_row.acip: DPER NA CHU SHING GI SDONG PO DAG CHA SHAS SU PHYE NA RANG BZHIN GYIS GRUB PA 'GA' YANG MED PA DE BZHIN DU RANG BZHIN GYIS GRUB MA GRUB RIGS PAS RNAM PAR DPYAD PA YIS BTZAL NA BDAG KYANG YANG DAG PAR GRUB PA MIN TE 'OG NAS 'CHAD PA'I BDAG MED SGRUB PA'I RIGS PAS GNOD PA'I PHYIR RO,
full_row.wylie: dper na chu shing gi sdong po dag cha shas su phye na rang bzhin gyis grub pa 'ga' yang med pa de bzhin du rang bzhin gyis grub ma grub rigs pas rnam par dpyad pa yis btsal na bdag kyang yang dag par grub pa min te 'og nas 'chad pa'i bdag med sgrub pa'i rigs pas gnod pa'i phyir ro
full_row.english: Think for example of a hollow reed: when you strip away the stem piece by piece, you find in the end that there is nothing with any nature at all. Here it's exactly the same: you use logic to try to find out whether things have any nature of their own or not, and come to the conclusion that there is no "myself" that you could ever correctly decide existed. The idea that such a self could exist is disproved totally by the various reasonings used, as I will describe below, to establish that nothing has any self-nature at all. 130 The Asian Classics Institute Course XVIII: The Great Ideas of Buddhism, Part Three Reading Four: The Guide to the Bodhisattva's Way of Life, Sixth of Six Parts The following contemplations are based on the Guide to the Bodhisattva's Way of Life (Bodhisattvacharyavatara; Byang-chub-sems-dpa'i spyod-pa la 'jug-pa) of the Buddhist master Shantideva (circa 700 AD), and the commentary upon it by Gyaltsab Je Darma Rinchen (1364-1432) entitled Entry Point for Children of the Victorious Buddhas (rGyal-sras 'jug-ngogs). The relevant sections are found at folios 33B-34A and 137B-140B, respectively, in the ACIP electronic editions TD3871 and S5436. full_row.acip: ,DES NA LUS ZHES PA'I THA SNYAD 'JUG PA'I GZHI LUS DE KHO RANG GI NGOS NAS JI LTAR YOD PA TSAL BA'I TSE SKYES BU'I RKANG PA DANG BYIN PA SKYES BU'I LUS MIN LA, BRLA DANG RKED PA'ANG LUS MA YIN LTO DANG RGYAB KYANG LUS MIN TE DE DAG LA BRTEN NAS SKYES BU'I LUS SU BTAGS PA'I PHYIR, BRANG DANG DPUNG PA'ANG LUS MA YIN LA RTZIB LOGS DANG LAG PA'ANG LUS MA YIN PA MCHAN KHUNG DANG PHRAG PA'ANG LUS MA YIN NANG KHROL RNAMS KYANG SKYES BU'I LUS DE MIN LA MGO DANG MGRIN PA'ANG SKYES BU'I LUS MIN NA YAN LAG 'DI RNAMS LA SKYES BU'I LUS NI GANG ZHIG YIN TE GANG YANG MIN LA, DE RNAMS TSOGS PA DANG DE RNAMS LAS NGO BO THA DAD PA YANG SKYES BU'I LUS MA YIN PAS LUS RANG BZHIN GYIS GRUB PA MED DO,
full_row.wylie: des na lus zhes pa'i tha snyad 'jug pa'i gzhi lus de kho rang gi ngos nas ji ltar yod pa tshal ba'i tshe skyes bu'i rkang pa dang byin pa skyes bu'i lus min la, brla dang rked pa'ang lus ma yin lto dang rgyab kyang lus min te de dag la brten nas skyes bu'i lus su btags pa'i phyir, brang dang dpung pa'ang lus ma yin la rtsib logs dang lag pa'ang lus ma yin pa mchan khung dang phrag pa'ang lus ma yin nang khrol rnams kyang skyes bu'i lus de min la mgo dang mgrin pa'ang skyes bu'i lus min na yan lag 'di rnams la skyes bu'i lus ni gang zhig yin te gang yang min la, de rnams tshogs pa dang de rnams las ngo bo tha dad pa yang skyes bu'i lus ma yin pas lus rang bzhin gyis grub pa med do
full_row.english: Suppose then that we seek the thing it is that we refer to with the word "body," looking for something which exists from its own side. Neither the foot nor the calf of a person is the body of the person, nor is the thigh or the waist. Neither as well is the front or the back of the body the body, for "body" is a concept applied to these things. The chest and the shoulders are not the body, nor are the ribcage or the arms. The side under the arm is not the body, and the shoulder above the arm is not the body. Nor are the inner organs the person's body. Nor finally is the head or the neck this person's body. Where then in any of these components would the body ever be? It is none of them. Neither is it the sum of these parts, nor is it something which is essentially separate from them. And so therefore the body is nothing that has any nature of its own. Contemplation Twenty-Eight The Emptiness of the Parts of Parts

full_row.acip: `GNYIS PA RANG LUGS BZHAG PA LA, BRLAN ZHING GSHER BA CHU PHOR PA GANG LA, LAS CAN GYI LHA MI YI DVAGS GSUM GYIS CIG CAR DU BLTAS PA DE'I TSE, CHU PHOR PA GANG PO DE DNGOS PO GSUM GYI GZHI MTHUN PA MA YIN PA DANG , DE'I TSE TSAD MTSUNGS GSUM NGES PAR MI DGOS SHING , BRLAN ZHING GSHER BA CHU PHOR PA GANG PO DE CHA SHAS GSUM LDAN DU SKYE BA DANG ,
full_row.wylie: `gnyis pa rang lugs bzhag pa la, brlan zhing gsher ba chu phor pa gang la, las can gyi lha mi yi dvags gsum gyis cig car du bltas pa de'i tshe, chu phor pa gang po de dngos po gsum gyi gzhi mthun pa ma yin pa dang , de'i tshe tshad mtshungs gsum nges par mi dgos shing , brlan zhing gsher ba chu phor pa gang po de cha shas gsum ldan du skye ba dang
full_row.english: Here secondly is the section where we establish our own position. Now suppose three different types of beings--a pleasure being, a human, and a craving spirit, each with their own karma--sit down together and look upon a glass filled with water, the thing we define as "wet and flowing." The glass of water is not at this point one thing which is simultaneously three different objects. Neither is it necessary in this situation for there to be three identical valid perceptions. And when the glass full of wet and flowing water occurs, it occurs with three different, distinct parts to it. [Translator's note: When the phrase "wet and flowing" (the definition of the element of water) is used here, it should be understood as emphasizing the more general concept of a liquid, rather than the water which the human perceives.]

full_row.english: There is, moreover, an example we can use for how, when the three different types of beings with their three karmas look all together at a glass full of something wet and flowing, there start to be three different objects, each confirmed by a valid perception. Suppose there is a ball of red-hot steel; one piece of this ball provides the material cause, and the "mantra of steel" provides a contributing factor. Due to these two, a person who has used the mantra of steel on his hand can touch the ball, but he doesn't undergo any sensation of heat; instead, he feels some other sensation. A person who has not used the mantra on his hand touches the ball and does feel a sensation of heat, and no other kind of sensation.

full_row.acip: SOS KA'I DUS SU ZLA BA'I REG BYA'I CHA SHAS GCIG GIS NYER LEN DANG , YI DVAGS KYI LAS KYIS LHAN CIG BYED RKYEN BYAS PA LA BRTEN NAS, DE'I LUS SHES KYI MYONG BYAR GYUR PA'I TSA BA'I REG BYA SKYE BA DANG , DGUN DUS SU NYI MA'I REG BYA'I CHA SHAS GCIG GIS NYER LEN DANG , YI DVAGS KYI LAS KYIS LHAN CIG BYED RKYEN BYAS PA LA BRTEN NAS, DE'I LUS SHES KYI MYONG BYAR GYUR PA'I GRANG BA'I REG BYA SKYE BA YOD PA LTA BU YIN PA'I PHYIR,
full_row.wylie: sos ka'i dus su zla ba'i reg bya'i cha shas gcig gis nyer len dang , yi dvags kyi las kyis lhan cig byed rkyen byas pa la brten nas, de'i lus shes kyi myong byar gyur pa'i tsha ba'i reg bya skye ba dang , dgun dus su nyi ma'i reg bya'i cha shas gcig gis nyer len dang , yi dvags kyi las kyis lhan cig byed rkyen byas pa la brten nas, de'i lus shes kyi myong byar gyur pa'i grang ba'i reg bya skye ba yod pa lta bu yin pa'i phyir
full_row.english: Another example would be the moon in springtime; one part of the feel of its rays on the body provides the material cause, and then the karma of a craving spirit provides a contributing factor. Based on these two, the spirit gets a sensation of heat, which is experienced by the consciousness of the body. So too with the wintertime sun; one part of the feel of its rays on the body provides the material cause, and then the karma of the craving spirit provides a contributing factor. Based on these two, the spirit gets a sensation cold, which is experienced by the consciousness of the body.

full_row.acip: DES NA, LAS CAN GYI 'GRO BA GSUM GYIS BRLAN ZHING GSHER BA PHOR PA GANG LA CIG CAR DU BLTAS PA DE'I TSE, TSAD MTSUNGS NGES PAR DGOS PA MA YIN TE, DGOS NA, PHOR PA GANG PO DE'I NANG DU GNAS KYI BLOS GNAS SHING , THA MAL GYI MIG SHES KYIS MI BZOD PA'I SROG CHAGS PHRA MO'I MIG SHES KYIS KYANG , DE'I TSAD MAR 'GRO DGOS PA DANG , RGYA MTSO'I NANG NA GNAS PA'I SROG CHAGS PHRA MO'I MIG SHES KYIS KYANG , RGYA MTSO'I TSAD LA TSAD MAR 'GRO DGOS PA DANG , LHA MA YIN 'GA' ZHIG LA, MTSON CHA PHOR GANG SNANG DGOS PA LA SOGS PA'I SKYON YOD PA'I PHYIR,
full_row.wylie: des na, las can gyi 'gro ba gsum gyis brlan zhing gsher ba phor pa gang la cig car du bltas pa de'i tshe, tshad mtshungs nges par dgos pa ma yin te, dgos na, phor pa gang po de'i nang du gnas kyi blos gnas shing , tha mal gyi mig shes kyis mi bzod pa'i srog chags phra mo'i mig shes kyis kyang , de'i tshad mar 'gro dgos pa dang , rgya mtsho'i nang na gnas pa'i srog chags phra mo'i mig shes kyis kyang , rgya mtsho'i tshad la tshad mar 'gro dgos pa dang , lha ma yin 'ga' zhig la, mtshon cha phor gang snang dgos pa la sogs pa'i skyon yod pa'i phyir
full_row.english: In conclusion now, let us consider again these three kinds of beings, each with their different karma, as they sit down together and look at a glass full of something wet and flowing. It's not necessarily true that they must all have valid perceptions which are identical. If they did, then the three beings looking at the glass of water would have to think of the water as a place to live, in the way that a creature living in water would. The three beings as well would have to see the water in the same way that microscopic organisms living in the water, little beings imperceptible to normal visual consciousness, see it with their own visual consciousness. Then too the visual consciousness of microscopic organisms living in the depths of the ocean would have to be a valid perception towards the entire extent of the sea. And certain kinds of near-gods too would have to see weapons as glasses of water, and on and on; the problems raised would be many.

full_row.wylie: de'i tshe na, tshad mtshungs nges par mi dgos kyang , tshad mtshungs gsum yod pa srid pa yin te, las kyi dbang gis dngos po tshad grub pa gsum bskyed nus pa sngar gyi rigs pas 'grub, de bskyed nus na, las kyi dbang gis snod tshad mtshungs gsum skye ba yod par yang mtshungs pa'i phyir
full_row.english: Again consider this same situation. Even though it is not necessarily true that the valid perceptions are identical, it is possible for there to be three valid perceptions here which happen to be identical. This is because, as we have already established logically, there can be a case where by the force of karma three different objects, each one confirmed by a valid perception, start to exist. And since this is possible, then it is equally possible that, by the force of karma, three equivalent valid perceptions of a vessel could start to exist as well. ************ When the text of the Essence of Eloquence was taught by Geshe Tupten Rinchen, he took great pains to point out that it is not correct--as some Western scholars have stated--that Je Tsongkapa himself adhered to the tenets of the Mind-Only School. The following selection to show that he follows, of course, the beliefs of the Consequence group is taken the concluding pages of our root text [ACIP electronic text S5396, ff. 112a-112b].

full_row.acip: DANG PO LA BEM SHES LDAN MIN 'DU BYED GSUM LAS, DANG PO LUS LTA BU LA MTSON NA DE YANG SHA RUS RDOS BCAS KYI YAN LAG LNGA TSOGS TZAM GYI LUS 'DI'I STENG DU, RTOG PAS BTAGS PA TZAM MA YIN PAR TSUGS THUB TU GRUB PA'I LUS YO RE BA ZHIG YOD PAR RANG CAG RNAMS LA BSNYON MED DU 'CHAR BA NI DGAG BYA'I SNANG TSUL YIN LA,
full_row.wylie: dang po la bem shes ldan min 'du byed gsum las, dang po lus lta bu la mtshon na de yang sha rus rdos bcas kyi yan lag lnga tshogs tsam gyi lus 'di'i steng du, rtog pas btags pa tsam ma yin par tshugs thub tu grub pa'i lus yo re ba zhig yod par rang cag rnams la bsnyon med du 'char ba ni dgag bya'i snang tshul yin la
full_row.english: For the first of these, we cover three different types of caused things: material things, mental things, and then changing things which are neither material nor mental.  To represent material things, we can take something like our own body. In actuality this body is nothing more than a collection of the five components [four limbs and a head]--nothing but flesh and bone in a certain configuration.  In actuality it's nothing more than a projection; but to us it appears as though it were, indisputably, some whole, discrete, and self-standing body. This is how the thing we deny appears to us.

full_row.acip: 'DI LA KHO NA RE, DE 'DRA BA'I MTSAN MED KYI RNAL 'BYOR DE SGOM STOBS KYIS STONG NYID MNGON SUM DU RTOGS PA'I TSE YANG BZHIN LAG GI RNAM PA CAN GYI LHA'I SKU SNANG BAR THAL, KHYOD KYI DAM BCA' 'THAD PA'I PHYIR NA MA KHYAB STE, KUN RDZOB PA'I LHA'I SKU MI SNANG YANG RGYUD GYI SGO NAS LHA'I RNAL 'BYOR DU 'JOG PA'I PHYIR,
full_row.wylie: 'di la kho na re, de 'dra ba'i mtshan med kyi rnal 'byor de sgom stobs kyis stong nyid mngon sum du rtogs pa'i tshe yang bzhin lag gi rnam pa can gyi lha'i sku snang bar thal, khyod kyi dam bca' 'thad pa'i phyir na ma khyab ste, kun rdzob pa'i lha'i sku mi snang yang rgyud gyi sgo nas lha'i rnal 'byor du 'jog pa'i phyir
full_row.english: At this point, someone might come and raise the following issue-- Suppose one does perform this deep practice where there are no more signs, as you've described it above, and then due to this meditation they manage to perceive emptiness directly.  Wouldn't the precious body of an Angel, complete with face and arms, be coming up in their mind at the very same time?  Because isn't your own position, in fact, correct? To this we answer, "It doesn't necessarily follow."  Because even though the precious body of an Angel which belongs to deceptive reality isn't in fact coming up in their mind at that point, we can still say that they are engaged in the deep practice of an Angel, as this practice is considered over a continuous length of time.

full_row.acip: YANG KHO NA RE, LTA BA DANG RGOD PA SOGS LAS BYUNG BA'I BDE BA GSUM GYIS STONG NYID RTOGS PA MED PAR THAL, DE DAG LAM DU BYED PA NI STONG NYID RTOGS PA'I YUL CAN KHYAD PAR CAN SKYED PA'I DON DU MA YIN PA'I PHYIR ZER NA DPYAD PAR BYA STE, RJES 'JUG PHAL CHER GYIS DE 'DRA YOD PAR BSHAD KYANG , RJE BDAG NYID CHEN PO'I LEGS BSHAD RNAMS SU DE LTAR GSAL BAR GSUNGS PA'I SHES BYED YOD MED TSOL DGOS PA'I PHYIR RO,,
full_row.wylie: yang kho na re, lta ba dang rgod pa sogs las byung ba'i bde ba gsum gyis stong nyid rtogs pa med par thal, de dag lam du byed pa ni stong nyid rtogs pa'i yul can khyad par can skyed pa'i don du ma yin pa'i phyir zer na dpyad par bya ste, rjes 'jug phal cher gyis de 'dra yod par bshad kyang , rje bdag nyid chen po'i legs bshad rnams su de ltar gsal bar gsungs pa'i shes byed yod med tshol dgos pa'i phyir ro
full_row.english: In response to all this, someone else may come and say, Are you saying then that we don't use the three different kinds of pleasure that we feel from looking into each other's eyes, flirting, and the rest to perceive emptiness?  Because you have stated that using these as a path is not something which is done in order to give rise to the extraordinary state of mind which perceives emptiness. Our reply is that this is a question which needs to be looked into further. full_row.english: Someone might come and make the following claim: Isn't it the case that there are no four forms each of bliss for the stages of where the element descends from the top, and then fills from below, where these are any one of the four forms of emptiness during the stage of transcendent mind? full_row.acip: MAS BRTAN LAS MA LANGS PA'I YAS BABS KYI DGA' GZHI NI SNGA MA'I MAS BRTAN LAS BDE BA CHE ZHING , BZHI KA LHAN SKYES SU 'JOG DGOS PA DANG , MAS BRTAN LAS LANGS PA'I RJES SU SKYES PA'I YAS BABS KYI DGA' BZHI NI SNGA MA LAS BDE BA CHE BA DANG BZHI KA LHAN SKYES YIN PA'I NGES PA MED PAR GSUNGS LA,
full_row.wylie: mas brtan las ma langs pa'i yas babs kyi dga' gzhi ni snga ma'i mas brtan las bde ba che zhing , bzhi ka lhan skyes su 'jog dgos pa dang , mas brtan las langs pa'i rjes su skyes pa'i yas babs kyi dga' bzhi ni snga ma las bde ba che ba dang bzhi ka lhan skyes yin pa'i nges pa med par gsungs la
full_row.english: It is stated that the four forms of bliss associated with the descent of the element from the top--the ones that occur after one has come out of the filling from the bottom--are more blissful than those of this previous filling from the bottom; all four would have to be considered simultaneous bliss. full_row.acip: DBANG BZHI THOB PA NI SMIN LAM DU 'JUG ZIN PAS NA 'JUG RUNG DU MI 'GRO BA'I PHYIR DE LTAR BZHAG PA MI 'THAD PAR STAG PHU BSTAN PA'I RGYAL MTSAN SOGS RANG PHYOGS KYI MKHAS GRUB TSAD LDAN MANG POS GSUNGS PAS, 'DIR RANG LUGS GONG DU BSHAD PA LTAR SMIN LAM 'JUG RUNG DBANG BZHI MA THOB BA NYID LA 'JOG DGOS,
full_row.wylie: dbang bzhi thob pa ni smin lam du 'jug zin pas na 'jug rung du mi 'gro ba'i phyir de ltar bzhag pa mi 'thad par stag phu bstan pa'i rgyal mtshan sogs rang phyogs kyi mkhas grub tshad ldan mang pos gsungs pas, 'dir rang lugs gong du bshad pa ltar smin lam 'jug rung dbang bzhi ma thob ba nyid la 'jog dgos
full_row.english: The fact is though that, once one receives the four empowerments, they have already entered the path that ripens us, so you can't say that they have made them fit to enter it.  Asserting that they do is incorrect, as many unerring and accomplished masters of our own school, such as Tenpay Gyeltsen of Takpu and others, have stated.  Therefore on this question we must adhere to the position we stated above, and establish a person as being fit to enter the path that ripens only if they have not received the four empowerments.

full_row.acip: SBYANG GZHI SBYONG BA LA RNAM PA MTHUN PAS SBYONG BA DANG, MI MTHUN PAS SBYONG BA GNYIS LAS, 'DIR DANG PO STE, BAR DO BAS MA DAG PA'I SKYE BA LEN PA DANG CHOS MTSUNGS PAR SGYU LUS PA DES PHUNG PO RNYING PAR 'JUG PA SOGS GZHI LAM 'BRAS GSUM THAMS CAD DU RNAM PA SHIN TU MTHUN,
full_row.wylie: sbyang gzhi sbyong ba la rnam pa mthun pas sbyong ba dang, mi mthun pas sbyong ba gnyis las, 'dir dang po ste, bar do bas ma dag pa'i skye ba len pa dang chos mtshungs par sgyu lus pa des phung po rnying par 'jug pa sogs gzhi lam 'bras gsum thams cad du rnam pa shin tu mthun
full_row.english: Generally speaking, there are two ways that you can purify a thing: with something comparable to it, or with something opposed to it.  Here we are talking about the first way.  When the practitioner who has reached the body of illusion goes into their old body, for example, this is comparable to a person in the inbetween state who then takes a new and impure birth.  This follows for the other two events as well, and so all three conditions here--the original state of things, the path, and the final result--are perfectly comparable to one another.

full_row.acip: MDOR NA BDE MCHOG LHA DRUG CU RE GNYIS RTEN DANG BRTEN PAR BCAS PA KHA tV'Am GA LA TSANG ZHING, DE THAMS CAD KYANG GTZO BO LAS RGYUD THA DAD PA MA YIN GYI GTZO BO'I YE SHES KHO NA'I CHA SHAS LAS GRUB PAS DE'I RNAM 'GYUR YIN PAS NA YAB MTSON ZHING SBAS PA'I TSUL GYIS 'DZIN PA'O, ,
full_row.wylie: mdor na bde mchog lha drug cu re gnyis rten dang brten par bcas pa kha TvAM ga la tshang zhing, de thams cad kyang gtso bo las rgyud tha dad pa ma yin gyi gtso bo'i ye shes kho na'i cha shas las grub pas de'i rnam 'gyur yin pas na yab mtshon zhing sbas pa'i tshul gyis 'dzin pa'o,
full_row.english: To put it briefly, the entire secret world of Highest Bliss--the 62 beings and the places where they stay--are all complete in this khatvanga.  None of these beings is a separate person from the central figure, but rather they are literally made of nothing more than a piece of His wisdom--and are thus His expression.  And so the staff represents the Man, and She holds Him in a way which is hidden from others.

full_row.acip: LUS LA LHA BSGOM PA TZAM GYIS LUS DKYIL MA YIN TE, DPER NA SKYE MCHED BZHIN YIN PAR GSUNGS KYANG, SA DGE'I YIG CHA PHAL MO CHER MA THON PA MAN NGAG LA YOD SHAG DANG, RANG GI LUS KYI CHA SHAS KYIS LHAN CIG BYED PA'I RKYEN DANG, SNGAGS PHRENG GIS NYE BAR LEN PA'I RGYU BYAS PA LA BRTEN NAS 'BYUNG BA YIN TE,
full_row.wylie: lus la lha bsgom pa tsam gyis lus dkyil ma yin te, dper na skye mched bzhin yin par gsungs kyang, sa dge'i yig cha phal mo cher ma thon pa man ngag la yod shag dang, rang gi lus kyi cha shas kyis lhan cig byed pa'i rkyen dang, sngags phreng gis nye bar len pa'i rgyu byas pa la brten nas 'byung ba yin te
full_row.english: It is not the case that something is the practice of the secret world of the body just because you visualize Angels inside of your body.  For example, some people have said that the secret world of the body is important simply because you use the physical parts of your body.  Although the majority of both the Sakya tradition and the Way of the Pure fail to bring out the reason why this practice is so profound, the point is made in the oral advices of our Lamas.  The secret world of the body arises from the contributing factor of the various parts of your own body, and the material cause of the string of secret words.

full_row.acip: 'O NA JI LTAR YIN ZHE NA, RANG RDO RJE 'CHANG DU GNAS PA DE LAS THA MAL PA'I LUS KYI CHA SHAS RE CHAD NAS THIM PAS GZHAL YAS KHANG SKAD CIG GI SNGA MA DES NYE BAR LEN PA'I RGYU DANG, SKAD CIG PHYI MA RANG GI LUS DES LHAN CIG BYED PA'I RKYEN BYAS NAS GRUB PA LTAR RO,
full_row.wylie: 'o na ji ltar yin zhe na, rang rdo rje 'chang du gnas pa de las tha mal pa'i lus kyi cha shas re chad nas thim pas gzhal yas khang skad cig gi snga ma des nye bar len pa'i rgyu dang, skad cig phyi ma rang gi lus des lhan cig byed pa'i rkyen byas nas grub pa ltar ro
full_row.english: How then are we supposed to do this practice? full_row.english: The upper ends of these three channels--the channel of taste, the solitary channel, and the central channel--extend straight up through the middle of the body; then the tip bends down a bit until it reaches the level of the spot between the eyebrows, where they then go down a little to the right and left. full_row.english: Now the scriptures state that the red element flows through the channel of taste, and that the white element flows through the solitary channel. full_row.english: In the fourth and fifth months, the limbs are completely distinct, like the two different Ramas. full_row.acip: GZHAN YANG DE'I CHA SHAS ('JIG RTEN) NI SO SO SKYE BO DANG, ('JIG RTEN LAS 'DAS) PA 'PHAGS PA RNAMS TE MDOR NA (RANG) DANG (GZHAN GYI) LUS NGAG YID KYI (SGO GSUM) DU BSAGS PA'I (DGE BA'I ME TOG) GI TSOGS LTA BU (CI YANG BKRA) BA STE SNA TSOGS PA CIR YANG MDZES PAR SNANG BA DANG,
full_row.wylie: gzhan yang de'i cha shas ('jig rten) ni so so skye bo dang, ('jig rten las 'das) pa 'phags pa rnams te mdor na (rang) dang (gzhan gyi) lus ngag yid kyi (sgo gsum) du bsags pa'i (dge ba'i me tog) gi tshogs lta bu (ci yang bkra) ba ste sna tshogs pa cir yang mdzes par snang ba dang
full_row.english: And this goodness can as well be divided into that of this world--that is, that accomplished by normal beings--and that which is beyond this world: accomplished by realized beings. full_row.acip: CHOS THAMS CAD RTOG PAS BTAGS PA'I DPE NI, THAG PA KHRA BO YUL MI GSAL BA NA GNAS PA'I TSE KHA CIG LA 'DI SBRUL LO SNYAM PA'I BLO 'BYUNG NGO, ,DE'I TSE THAG PA DE'I TSOGS PA DANG CHA SHAS GANG YANG SBRUL DU MED KYANG, DE LA SBRUL LO SNYAM PA'I SBRUL NI RTOG PAS BTAGS PA TZAM DU 'CHAR RO,,
full_row.wylie: chos thams cad rtog pas btags pa'i dpe ni, thag pa khra bo yul mi gsal ba na gnas pa'i tshe kha cig la 'di sbrul lo snyam pa'i blo 'byung ngo, ,de'i tshe thag pa de'i tshogs pa dang cha shas gang yang sbrul du med kyang, de la sbrul lo snyam pa'i sbrul ni rtog pas btags pa tsam du 'char ro
full_row.english: There is a metaphor used to describe how all existing things are labeled with our concepts. When you put a rope with a checkered pattern on it in a dark corner, some people might get the impression that it's a snake. The truth at this point though is that nothing about the rope is a snake: neither the rope as a whole, nor the parts of the rope. Nonetheless the person thinks of the rope as a snake, and this snake is an example of something which only makes its appearance as something labeled with a concept.

full_row.acip: DE BZHIN DU PHUNG PO 'DI LA BRTEN NAS NGA'O SNYAM DU 'BYUNG YANG, PHUNG PO'I TSOGS PA DANG RGYUN DANG CHA SHAS GANG YANG NGA'I MTSAN GZHIR 'JOG RGYU MED CING, PHUNG PO LAS NGO BO THA DAD PA GZHAN ZHIG KYANG NGA'I MTSAN GZHIR BZUNG MED PAS, NGA DE NI PHUNG PO LA BRTEN NAS BTAGS PA TZAM YIN GYI, RANG GI NGO BO NYID KYIS GRUB PA MED DO,,
full_row.wylie: de bzhin du phung po 'di la brten nas nga'o snyam du 'byung yang, phung po'i tshogs pa dang rgyun dang cha shas gang yang nga'i mtshan gzhir 'jog rgyu med cing, phung po las ngo bo tha dad pa gzhan zhig kyang nga'i mtshan gzhir bzung med pas, nga de ni phung po la brten nas btags pa tsam yin gyi, rang gi ngo bo nyid kyis grub pa med do
full_row.english: In the same way, the heaps of parts that make us up serve as a basis for us to get the impression "This is me." There is nothing at all about these heaps as a whole, nor their continuation over time, nor their separate components, that we could establish as being an actual representation of "me." At the same time though there is nothing else, nothing essentially separate from these heaps of parts to ourselves, that we could consider an actual representation of "me" either. As such, this "me" is merely something labeled upon the heaps of parts that make us up; there is nothing which exists by its own essence.

full_row.acip: ON KYANG MA BRTAG MA DPYAD PA'I BLO NGO NA YOD PAS THA SNYAD DU ZHING GI BKOD PA RNAMS ZHES BYA'O, ,SANGS RGYAS KYI ZHING DU MA ZAD, SNOD BCUD KYI BKOD PA THAMS CAD KYANG CHA SHAS DU MA TSOGS PA LA BTAGS PA STE, KHANG PA LA SOGS PA BZHIN NO, ,DE DAG THAMS CAD KYANG RIGS PAS RDUL PHRA RAB KYI BAR BSHIG NA CI YANG MA YIN PA'I BAR 'GYUR TE MTSON TZAM
full_row.wylie: on kyang ma brtag ma dpyad pa'i blo ngo na yod pas tha snyad du zhing gi bkod pa rnams zhes bya'o, ,sangs rgyas kyi zhing du ma zad, snod bcud kyi bkod pa thams cad kyang cha shas du ma tshogs pa la btags pa ste, khang pa la sogs pa bzhin no, ,de dag thams cad kyang rigs pas rdul phra rab kyi bar bshig na ci yang ma yin pa'i bar 'gyur te mtshon tsam
full_row.english: MO,,Since though they do exist to that state of mind which performs no check or analysis, we can nominally call them "paradise." This fact refers not only to the paradise of a Buddha, but also to each and every thing which has ever been put here: to both the world where beings live, and to the beings who live in the world. All of these are simply a label put on the collection of a number of parts: they are all the same as a house, for example. And all of these are such that, should you break them down mentally all the way to their tiniest atoms, you would reach the point where they are nothing at all. (This is the briefest sketch of the meaning for you.)

full_row.english: Now admittedly all the elements listed here are metaphorical; but we can say that "part" refers to greater or lesser components. "Countable" means this many more or less; "example" is a reference to different illustrations. full_row.acip: SHES BYA'AM DNGOS PO LA DBYE NA, BDEN PA GNYIS SU YOD, BCOM PA'AM BLOS CHA SHAS SO SOR GSAL BA NA RANG 'DZIN GYI BLO 'DOR DU RUNG BA'I CHOS RNAMS NI KUN RDZOB BDEN PA YIN LA,

full_row.english: They assert that all knowable things—which then is to say, all functioning things—can be divided into two different realities.  The first one, deceptive reality, they describe as consisting of all of those objects which exist in a way such that—when they are destroyed, or broken down by the mind into their various constituent parts—then the state of mind which holds them must also fade away.

full_row.acip: BDEN 'DZIN GYI YUL SUN PHYUNG BA'I LTA BA MA RNYED PA'I RGYUD LA, BDEN BRDZUN GANG GIS KYANG KHYAD PAR DU MA BYAS PA'I PHUNG PO LA DMIGS NAS, DE GNYIS GANG GIS KYANG KHYAD PAR DU MA BYAS PA'I MI RTAG PA SOGS SU THA SNYAD PA'I TSAD MAS GRUB PA DU MA ZHIG 'ONG LA, SGOM PA'I TSE YANG DON DE BSGOMS PAS SNGAR BSHAD PA BZHIN GYI LAM RGYUD LA SKYE'O,,
full_row.wylie: bden 'dzin gyi yul sun phyung ba'i lta ba ma rnyed pa'i rgyud la, bden brdzun gang gis kyang khyad par du ma byas pa'i phung po la dmigs nas, de gnyis gang gis kyang khyad par du ma byas pa'i mi rtag pa sogs su tha snyad pa'i tshad mas grub pa du ma zhig 'ong la, sgom pa'i tshe yang don de bsgoms pas sngar bshad pa bzhin gyi lam rgyud la skye'o
full_row.english: The mind of this person—one who has yet to arrive at the viewpoint in which the object of the tendency to hold things as real has been demolished—is focusing on the parts of the person and failing to make any distinction at all between what is real & what is false. And since when they then meditate they are meditating on these particular kinds of facts, the path that arises in their mind looks like the one we described above.

full_row.english: What does it mean then when we say that a person has “rid oneself of a belief in objects of the mind—outer objects”? full_row.acip: DE LA SKYES BU NI GANG ZAG DANG SEMS CAN DANG NGA DANG BDAG GO ,SA MIN NAS RNAM SHES MA YIN PA'I BAR GYIS SEMS CAN GYI KHAMS DRUG GI CHA SHAS DANG, KUN MIN GYIS KHAMS KYI TSOGS PA GANG YANG GANG ZAG TU 'JOG PA BKAG GO ,TSIG THA MAS KHAMS LAS NGO BO THA DAD PA GANG ZAG TU 'JOG PA BKAG GO
full_row.wylie: de la skyes bu ni gang zag dang sems can dang nga dang bdag go ,sa min nas rnam shes ma yin pa'i bar gyis sems can gyi khams drug gi cha shas dang, kun min gyis khams kyi tshogs pa gang yang gang zag tu 'jog pa bkag go ,tshig tha mas khams las ngo bo tha dad pa gang zag tu 'jog pa bkag go
full_row.english: The word “individual” here refers to the person; or the living being; the “I” or the “self.” The list of what it is not—which goes from “earth” up to “consciousness”—refers to the parts of a living being: the six elements which make them up. The phrase “none of these” is meant to deny that there is any combination of these elements which we can posit as being the person. full_row.acip: DE LAS GZHAN PA'I STONG TSUL RNAMS RANG GI NGO BOS STONG PA MIN PA'I RGYU MTSAN NI, STONG TSUL SNGA MA TSAD MAS GRUB ZIN BYED PA MA NYAMS PA'I RING LA, GRUB MTHAS GZHI DE BDEN PA'AM DE'I DON DU YOD PAR 'DZIN PA'I SGRO 'DOGS SKYE MI SRID LA, PHYI MA RNAMS KYI DON TSAD MAS GRUB CING BYED PA MA NYAMS KYANG, GRUB MTHA' BDEN PA'AM BDEN PA'I DON DU SGRO 'DOGS PA MI 'GAL BA'O,,
full_row.wylie: de las gzhan pa'i stong tshul rnams rang gi ngo bos stong pa min pa'i rgyu mtshan ni, stong tshul snga ma tshad mas grub zin byed pa ma nyams pa'i ring la, grub mthas gzhi de bden pa'am de'i don du yod par 'dzin pa'i sgro 'dogs skye mi srid la, phyi ma rnams kyi don tshad mas grub cing byed pa ma nyams kyang, grub mtha' bden pa'am bden pa'i don du sgro 'dogs pa mi 'gal ba'o
full_row.english: And what then is the reason why we say that ways in which things could be empty that are different than these particular ways do not represent an emptiness of some kind of self-essence? Suppose that those previous ways in which we described things as being empty had already been confirmed by accurate perception; and we were all still sitting in a place where none of those confirmations had in any way declined. It would in that state be impossible for us to hold a school of thought which took those same examples of things to exist in truth; neither would it be possible for there to grow, within our minds, that form of overestimation where we held that things could exist in this same kind of truth. The idea in the latter cases here would be that a certain point had been confirmed by an accurate perception, and that the working of this perception had in no way declined; and yet this would not preclude overestimation through a learned philosophical school which said that a certain object was real; or even described what it was to be real. Normal reality cannot stand up under true analysis

full_row.acip: LUGS DANG PO LA NI, MYU GU LTA BU'I DNGOS PO CIG ZHIG PA NA, MYU GU'I CHA SHAS KYI DNGOS PO THAMS CAD NI LOG LA, MYU GU LAS GZHAN PA BUM PA LA SOGS PA'I DNGOS PO GZHAN GANG YANG MA THOB PAS, ZHIG PA DE DNGOS PO GTAN MIN PAR 'DOD DE, SNGON PO LA SOGS PA SKYE MCHED RE RE BA'I DNGOS PO DANG, BUM PA LA SOGS PA RANG GI CHA SHAS KYI DNGOS PO TSOGS PA GANG YANG ZHIG PA DE'I MTSAN GZHIR MI RUNG BA'I PHYIR DNGOS PO MIN NO SNYAM PA'O,,
full_row.wylie: lugs dang po la ni, myu gu lta bu'i dngos po cig zhig pa na, myu gu'i cha shas kyi dngos po thams cad ni log la, myu gu las gzhan pa bum pa la sogs pa'i dngos po gzhan gang yang ma thob pas, zhig pa de dngos po gtan min par 'dod de, sngon po la sogs pa skye mched re re ba'i dngos po dang, bum pa la sogs pa rang gi cha shas kyi dngos po tshogs pa gang yang zhig pa de'i mtshan gzhir mi rung ba'i phyir dngos po min no snyam pa'o
full_row.english: According to the first of these two positions, when a functional thing like a sprout comes to an end, all the functional entities which constitute component parts of the sprout are cancelled. At the same time, no entity other than the sprout—nothing like a water pitcher or the like—is thus actualized; and, as such, they have to say that there cannot be the slightest functional thing left here. What they are thinking is that there is nothing at all that would be fitting to point to as a classical example of this kind of stopping—neither the functional things represented by the individual doors of sense such as blue or the like; nor functioning things which are conglomerates of their components, as in the case of pitchers or the like. As such, they would say, the stopping could never itself be a functional thing.

full_row.acip: CHOS THAMS CAD RTOG PAS BTAGS PA'I DPE NI, THAG PA KHRA BO YUL MI GSAL BA NA GNAS PA'I TSE KHA CIG LA 'DI SBRUL LO SNYAM PA'I BLO 'BYUNG NGO, ,DE'I TSE THAG PA DE'I TSOGS PA DANG CHA SHAS GANG YANG SBRUL DU MED KYANG, DE LA SBRUL LO SNYAM PA'I SBRUL NI RTOG PAS BTAGS PA TZAM DU 'CHAR RO,,
full_row.wylie: chos thams cad rtog pas btags pa'i dpe ni, thag pa khra bo yul mi gsal ba na gnas pa'i tshe kha cig la 'di sbrul lo snyam pa'i blo 'byung ngo, ,de'i tshe thag pa de'i tshogs pa dang cha shas gang yang sbrul du med kyang, de la sbrul lo snyam pa'i sbrul ni rtog pas btags pa tsam du 'char ro
full_row.english: There is a metaphor used to describe how all existing things are labeled with our concepts. When you put a rope with a checkered pattern on it in a dark corner, some people might get the impression that it's a snake. The truth at this point though is that nothing about the rope is a snake: neither the rope as a whole, nor the parts of the rope. Nonetheless the person thinks of the rope as a snake, and this snake is an example of something which only makes its appearance as something labeled with a concept.

full_row.acip: DE BZHIN DU PHUNG PO 'DI LA BRTEN NAS NGA'O SNYAM DU 'BYUNG YANG, PHUNG PO'I TSOGS PA DANG RGYUN DANG CHA SHAS GANG YANG NGA'I MTSAN GZHIR 'JOG RGYU MED CING, PHUNG PO LAS NGO BO THA DAD PA GZHAN ZHIG KYANG NGA'I MTSAN GZHIR BZUNG MED PAS, NGA DE NI PHUNG PO LA BRTEN NAS BTAGS PA TZAM YIN GYI, RANG GI NGO BO NYID KYIS GRUB PA MED DO,,
full_row.wylie: de bzhin du phung po 'di la brten nas nga'o snyam du 'byung yang, phung po'i tshogs pa dang rgyun dang cha shas gang yang nga'i mtshan gzhir 'jog rgyu med cing, phung po las ngo bo tha dad pa gzhan zhig kyang nga'i mtshan gzhir bzung med pas, nga de ni phung po la brten nas btags pa tsam yin gyi, rang gi ngo bo nyid kyis grub pa med do
full_row.english: In the same way, the heaps of parts that make us up serve as a basis for us to get the impression “This is me.” There is nothing at all about these heaps as a whole, nor their continuation over time, nor their separate components, that we could establish as being an actual representation of “me.” At the same time though there is nothing else, nothing essentially separate from these heaps of parts to ourselves, that we could consider an actual representation of “me” either. As such, this “me” is merely something labeled upon the heaps of parts that make us up; there is nothing which exists by its own essence.

(This is the briefest sketch of the meaning for you.)

full_row.acip: DE YANG RGYU RKYEN DANG CHA SHAS LA BRTEN NAS 'BYUNG NA GZHAN DBANG GIS SAM GZHAN LA RAG LAS PA'I DBANG GIS BYUNG BA YIN GYI, RANG DBANG GIS SAM GZHAN LA BLTOS MED DU BYUNG BA YIN {%MIN} PAS NA RANG BZHIN GYIS MED PA YIN TE, BZHI BRGYA PA LAS,
full_row.wylie: de yang rgyu rkyen dang cha shas la brten nas 'byung na gzhan dbang gis sam gzhan la rag las pa'i dbang gis byung ba yin gyi, rang dbang gis sam gzhan la bltos med du byung ba yin {%min} pas na rang bzhin gyis med pa yin te, bzhi brgya pa las
full_row.english: And the list goes on and on. full_row.acip: BDAG MED PA LA BDAG TU 'DZIN PA NI PHYIN CI LOG TU BSHAD PA'I PHYIR BDAG 'DZIN NAM BDEN 'DZIN YANG PHYIN CI LOG TU 'JOG DGOS PAS, PHYIN CI LOG ZHES PA TZAM GYIS PHYIN CI LOG BZHI KA LA NGES PAR BSHAD DGOS PA NI MA YIN NO,,
full_row.wylie: bdag med pa la bdag tu 'dzin pa ni phyin ci log tu bshad pa'i phyir bdag 'dzin nam bden 'dzin yang phyin ci log tu 'jog dgos pas, phyin ci log zhes pa tsam gyis phyin ci log bzhi ka la nges par bshad dgos pa ni ma yin no
full_row.english: Now it is explained that to take something which has no nature of its own to have some such nature is a “backwards thought”; as such, we'd have to say that the belief that things have a self-nature, which could also be called the belief that things are real, would have itself to be considered a backwards thought. But it's not the case that just because something has been referred to as a “backwards thought,” then we'd have to say that all four backwards thoughts were involved.

full_row.acip: SANGS RGYAS KYI BKA' YIN NA ZHAL NAS GSUNGS DGOS PA'I NGES PA MED DE, GDUGS DKAR NI SANGS RGYAS KYI GTZUG TOR NAS BYUNG ZHING, DER MA ZAD, SANGS RGYAS KYI MDZOD SPU MGRIN PA SPYAN SNYAN SHANGS LA SOGS PA'I SKU'I CHA SHAS THAMS CAD DANG LJON PAR {%PA} DAG LAS KYANG CHOS STON NUS PA'I PHYIR TE,
full_row.wylie: sangs rgyas kyi bka' yin na zhal nas gsungs dgos pa'i nges pa med de, gdugs dkar ni sangs rgyas kyi gtsug tor nas byung zhing, der ma zad, sangs rgyas kyi mdzod spu mgrin pa spyan snyan shangs la sogs pa'i sku'i cha shas thams cad dang ljon par {%pa} dag las kyang chos ston nus pa'i phyir te
full_row.english: Something can be the word of a Buddha, and not necessarily have to be spoken from his or her holy lips. The secret teachings of the White Parasol, for example, issued from the crest upon the Buddha's head. And not only that—all the different parts of a Buddha's body also have the ability to grant teachings: the instruction can come from the sacred hair on his or her forehead; from the front of their throat; from their ears; and even from their anus or other places. The teachings of the Buddha can even come from the sound of the trees of the forest, blowing in the wind.

full_row.english: The same thing happens when we look at our body and mind—the heaps that make us up—and the thought comes up in our head, “That's me!” There is nothing about the color of these heaps, or about their shape, or the successive moments of their flow, or the various components, or their various parts, or the combined construct of earlier and later versions, or their flow itself, or anything else at all, which could properly be considered what we call “me.” And that's because it would be illogical.

full_row.acip: BYIN GYIS RLOBS ZHES PA GZI BYIN SGYUR CES PA STE RANG RGYUD SKAD CIG SNGA MA NYON, MONGS DANG MTSUNGS LDAN DU SONG BA'I BLO PHYIN CI LOG TU YOD PA DE SKAD CIG PHYI MAR BLA, MA LA DAD GUS CHEN PO'I SLO NAS TSUL BZHIN DU BRTEN NUS PA DANG LAM YONGS RDZOGS PHYIN CI MA LOG PA RGYUD LA LDAN PA'I SKAL BA CAN DU SGYUR BAR MDZOD CIG CES GSOL BA BTAB PA STE 'DI 'OG MA RNAMS LA'ANG 'GRE GSUNGS
full_row.wylie: byin gyis rlobs zhes pa gzi byin sgyur ces pa ste rang rgyud skad cig snga ma nyon, mongs dang mtshungs ldan du song ba'i blo phyin ci log tu yod pa de skad cig phyi mar bla, ma la dad gus chen po'i slo nas tshul bzhin du brten nus pa dang lam yongs rdzogs phyin ci ma log pa rgyud la ldan pa'i skal ba can du sgyur bar mdzod cig ces gsol ba btab pa ste 'di 'og ma rnams la'ang 'gre gsungs
full_row.english: The words "bless me" here mean "embellish me"; which is to say, "transform the condition of my mind." A minute ago my mind was twisted wrong, and joined with every kind of bad thought. Now, in the very next moment, may I be blessed with the good fortune of being able to find and follow my Lama properly, with every reverence; may my mind be straightened, and become filled with each and every Step of the path. This is the thing I ask, my Lama. The explanation of the words "bless me" here applies as well to each of the other verses in which they appear. Asian Classics Institute Reading Two: Getting the Essence of Life III. Advice to Take the Essence of Life

archive_object.english: Someone might make the following claim: Isn't it true that when all those beings sit down together and look at something, there isn't any actual pus and blood at all? Because isn't it true first of all that, when a person with cataracts looks into a porcelain basin, there is no strand of hair in the basin at all? And, secondly, doesn't [Master Dharmakirti's] text itself say, Identical to the case of someone where his sense power has a cataract, Is the mind of a craving spirit as well, which sees a stream of water as pus.

full_row.english: Again consider this same situation. This is because, as we have already established logically, there can be a case where by the force of karma three different objects, each one confirmed by a valid perception, start to exist. full_row.acip: RNAG LA SOGS PA'I DNGOS PO GSUM PO DE SPYIR GO SA 'GOG NUS KYI DNGOS PO YIN, KYANG DE LTAR BLTAS PA DE'I TSE NA GO SA 'GOG BYED KYI DNGOS PO MA YIN PA MI 'GAL TE RI RAB GRU BZHI DANG ZLUM PO LA SOGS PA PHAN TSUN GO SA 'GOG NUS KYI DNGOS PO YIN KYANG RI RAB GCIG GI GO SA NA DE GNYIS KA YOD PA SRID PA LTA BU YIN PA'I PHYIR LCAGS GONG DMAR 'BAR BA TSA BA YIN KYANG LCAGS SNGAGS BTAB PA'I LAG PAS REG PA'I TSE DE'I MYONG BYAR GYUR PA'I REG BYA DE TSA BA'I REG BYA MA YIN TE TSA BA MA YIN PA'I REG BYA YIN PA'I PHYIR
full_row.wylie: rnag la sogs pa'i dngos po gsum po de spyir go sa 'gog nus kyi dngos po yin, kyang de ltar bltas pa de'i tshe na go sa 'gog byed kyi dngos po ma yin pa mi 'gal te ri rab gru bzhi dang zlum po la sogs pa phan tshun go sa 'gog nus kyi dngos po yin kyang ri rab gcig gi go sa na de gnyis ka yod pa srid pa lta bu yin pa'i phyir lcags gong dmar 'bar ba tsha ba yin kyang lcags sngags btab pa'i lag pas reg pa'i tshe de'i myong byar gyur pa'i reg bya de tsha ba'i reg bya ma yin te tsha ba ma yin pa'i reg bya yin pa'i phyir
full_row.english: Generally speaking, each of the three objects mentioned—the pus and the other two—are things of the type that block other objects from entering into the space which they themselves occupy. It is no contradiction though to say that, in this situation where the beings are looking this way, they are not objects such that they block other things from entering into the space they occupy. This is true for the following reason. A central mountain of the world which is square in shape, and a central mountain of the world which is round in shape, and the like, are objects such that they block other things from entering the space they occupy. Nevertheless, it is possible for both these things to occupy the space taken up by a single central mountain of the world. A red-hot ball of steel is something that's hot, but consider what happens when a person touches it after he has used the mantra of steel on his hand. The sensation that he feels is not a sensation of heat; on the contrary, it is a sensation of something not heat. [This concludes the section of the text entitled "The Stream."] The Asian Classics Institute Reading Three: Emptiness and Paradise; Emptiness and Purification The root text is An Exalted Sutra of the Greater Way on the Perfection of Wisdom, entitled The Diamond Cutter, and is found in bold in the translation and is marked with an ornament in the Tibetan. The commentary is by Choney Lama Drakpa Shedrup (1675-1748) of Sera Mey Tibetan Monastery.

full_row.acip: RNAM BSHAD DGONGS PA RAB GSAL LAS RIGS PA DRUG CU PA'I 'GREL PAR MYANG, 'DAS KUN RDZOB BDEN PAR GSUNGS PA'I DON MYANG 'DAS DON DAM PA'I BDEN PAR YOD PA BLO KUN RDZOB PA LA BLTOS NAS 'JOG DGOS PA'I DON DU GSUNGS PA DANG DRANG NGES RNAM 'BYED LAS KYANG CHOS NYID CHOS NYID DU GRUB PAR GSUNGS PA DANG BSKAL BZANG MIG 'BYED LAS KYANG GNAS LUGS SU GRUB PA TZAM GYIS DON DAM PAR GRUB MI DGOS PAR GSUNGS PA'I PHYIR
full_row.wylie: rnam bshad dgongs pa rab gsal las rigs pa drug cu pa'i 'grel par myang, 'das kun rdzob bden par gsungs pa'i don myang 'das don dam pa'i bden par yod pa blo kun rdzob pa la bltos nas 'jog dgos pa'i don du gsungs pa dang drang nges rnam 'byed las kyang chos nyid chos nyid du grub par gsungs pa dang bskal bzang mig 'byed las kyang gnas lugs su grub pa tsam gyis don dam par grub mi dgos par gsungs pa'i phyir
full_row.english: And this is true first of all because the Perfect Explanation, an Illumination of the True Thought, states that—when the commentary to the Sixty Verses of Reasoning describes nirvana as deceptive reality—what it means is that nirvana must be established as existing as ultimate reality with reference toa deceived state of mind. Distinguishing between the Figurative and the Literal alsostates that the real nature of things exists as the real nature of things; and Opening the Eyes of the Good and Fortune states that it doesn't automatically mean that something exists ultimately just because it exists as the real nature of things.

full_row.acip: DE'I TSE NA 'GRO BA GSUM PO DE'I MIG SHES THAMS CAD TSAD MA YIN NAM 'GA' ZHIG TSAD, MA YIN PA DAG LAS GANG YIN DANG PO LTAR NA BRLAN ZHING GSHER BA CHU PHOR PA GANG PO DE, RNAG KHRAG LA SOGS PA'I DNGOS PO GSUM GA YIN PA DANG 'GAL BA LA MA 'KHRUL BA'I, TSAD MA YOD PA DANG PHOR PA GANG PO DE CHU YIN PA DANG CHU MA YIN PA GNYIS KAR TSAD MAS RTOGS PAR THAL DE'I TSE NA 'GRO BA GSUM PO DE'I MIG SHES THAMS CAD TSAD MA YIN PA'I PHYIR
full_row.wylie: de'i tshe na 'gro ba gsum po de'i mig shes thams cad tshad ma yin nam 'ga' zhig tshad, ma yin pa dag las gang yin dang po ltar na brlan zhing gsher ba chu phor pa gang po de, rnag khrag la sogs pa'i dngos po gsum ga yin pa dang 'gal ba la ma 'khrul ba'i, tshad ma yod pa dang phor pa gang po de chu yin pa dang chu ma yin pa gnyis kar tshad mas rtogs par thal de'i tshe na 'gro ba gsum po de'i mig shes thams cad tshad ma yin pa'i phyir
full_row.english: We ask you then a question: in the situation you've just described, is it that the visual consciousness of all three beings are a valid perception, or is it that only one or two of them are a valid perception? Suppose you say all three are valid. Well then, the glass of something wet and flowing, of water, must be full of something that is all three different things: pus and blood, and each of the others. And then too it must be possible for there to be multiple and yet still valid perceptions which see one thing in two completely incompatible ways. And finally there must be such a thing as a valid perception which correctly perceives that the glass is filled with something which is simultaneously water and yet not water. Why so? Because, according to your view, the three differing cases of visual consciousness possessed by the three different beings would all have to be

full_row.wylie: rgyas par zung du bsgrubs yod aang, ,cha shas tshogs pa'ang khyod min zhing, ,re re'ang khyod min khyod kyang min
full_row.english: You could go further and check Whether it goes both ways: The sum of all your parts is not you, Nor is it that any one part is you; And neither can we say That you are you! The grand, unifying picture of you is not you by itself either, without all the component pictures that it ties together.  Truly feeling that I am an individual—like everything else in the universe—depends on the appropriate picture for that feeling.  What would be the karmic cause—how would we have to treat others around us—to see this picture coming out of our mind, as the karmic seed opens? Mental parts & wholes

full_row.english: It would appear That those of the Mind-Only School And the Independent Group Hold presentations which say That the ideas that things Exist in and of themselves, Or exist by definition, Or exist through some nature of their own, Or exist substantially Are actually correct. The Mind-Only group is a step above both the Detailist and Sutrist schools, whom we've already heard from.  Their defining belief is that—when we are looking at a patch of blue—the blue which we see is not standing in the outside world; rather, we are watching a seed within our mind flower into a blue color which is also in our mind.  All of this seeing of the outside world is happening within a region of our own mind known as “storehouse consciousness.” The fourth and highest of the four schools of classical Buddhism is known as the “Middle Way.”  It is divided into two sections: the Independent Group, and the Consequence Group.  Members of the Independent Group believe that words, and logic, have an inborn capacity to express or prove things; which is to say, accurate words and correct logic should be perceived the same by any sane person. This then is what it means to say that these thinkers believe that some things could exist by definition, and so on—all the terms listed here refer to the same things.  Still though these opinions fail to allow for a world which is in every detail created by the seeds within our mind.

full_row.acip: ,NGA PHUNG BDEN PA'I GCIG GRUB NA, ,PHUNG PO'I CHA SHAS KUN DANG NI, ,BDEN PA'I GCIG TU GRUB DGOS PAS, ,SHAR NUB LHO BYANG DBUS DBYE BA'I, ,PHYOGS NI GANG DU GCIG PAR 'GYUR,
full_row.wylie: nga phung bden pa'i gcig grub na, ,phung po'i cha shas kun dang ni, ,bden pa'i gcig tu grub dgos pas, ,shar nub lho byang dbus dbye ba'i, ,phyogs ni gang du gcig par 'gyur
full_row.english: If the “me” were, In reality, One with my body & mind, Then the “me” would have to be, In reality, One with each and every one Of the separate parts of body & mind. And then the “me” would be One with each of the separate Directions of east, and west, South, and north, and middle. If I am—from my own side—equivalent to the sum of the parts of my body and mind, then I should equally be equivalent to the sum of each of their parts: hands and feet, sadness and happiness. The physical parts of me have further divisions into those to the left, and those to the right; or, we can say, corresponding for example to north and south.  A whole which existed from its own side would also have to include the extent of all the parts of each of the directions—and thus be as large as the universe itself.
